note.explanation: A body is balanced when the total clockwise moment about a point equals the total anticlockwise moment about that point. A moment is calculated by multiplying the force by its perpendicular distance from the pivot.
examples: A 10 N force acting 0.2 m from a pivot makes a moment of 10 × 0.2 = 2 N m.
If a 30 N force acts 0.4 m from a pivot, its moment is 30 × 0.4 = 12 N m.
note.checkAnswer: The clockwise and anticlockwise moments are equal.
note.simple: Think of a seesaw: a smaller force can balance a larger one if it acts farther from the pivot.
note.checkQuestion: What must be equal for a body to balance about a point?
note.title: Principle of Moments
steps: Choose the pivot or point about which the body turns.
Work out each moment using force × perpendicular distance from the pivot.
Separate the moments that turn clockwise from those that turn anticlockwise.
For balance, set total clockwise moments equal to total anticlockwise moments.
Solve the equation and include the correct unit.
note.answer: When a body is in balanced position, the sum of clockwise moments about any point equals the sum of anticlockwise moments about that point.

modelAnswer: When a body is in balanced position, the sum of clockwise moments about any point equals the sum of anticlockwise moments about that point.
Moment = force × perpendicular distance from the point.
For the balanced metre rule, w_1 × l_1 + w_2 × l_2 = w_3 × l_3.
The weights w_1 and w_2 produce anticlockwise moments, and w_3 produces a clockwise moment.
Therefore, total anticlockwise moments = total clockwise moments.

explain.title: Moment of a force
explain.body: A force can make a body turn about a point. In this example, each weight's moment is its weight multiplied by its distance from the centre of gravity.

explain.title: Turning directions
explain.body: Name each moment clockwise or anticlockwise about the pivot. In Activity 4.2, w_1 and w_2 turn the rule anticlockwise, while w_3 turns it clockwise.

explain.title: Principle of moments
explain.body: When a body is in balanced position, the sum of clockwise moments about any point equals the sum of anticlockwise moments about that point.

explain.title: Using the rule
explain.body: For a balanced metre rule, add the moments on each side and set the totals equal: w_1 × l_1 + w_2 × l_2 = w_3 × l_3.

mistakes: Using the full force at an angle instead of resolving it and using the component perpendicular to the stick.
Using the distance from the end of the object rather than the distance from the pivot.
Adding clockwise and anticlockwise moments together instead of setting their totals equal for balance.
Forgetting to convert centimetres to metres when the answer is required in N m.
Giving a numerical answer without a unit.
